item.title: A growing distorted plume at the Pacific LLVP’s margin
item.content:encoded:
Nature Geoscience, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41561-026-02151-6

Analysis of seismic waves has revealed a growing low-velocity structure in the deepest mantle beneath the Pacific Ocean; its strongly distorted shape may indicate vigorous convection in the region.
item.dc:title: A growing distorted plume at the Pacific LLVP’s margin

item.title: Chemical processing of sulfur dioxide enhances cloud sensitivity to aerosols
item.content:encoded:
Nature Geoscience, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41561-026-02140-9

The conversion of sulfur dioxide into aerosol particles greatly enhances the cooling effect of clouds by increasing concentrations of cloud condensation nuclei and cloud droplets, according to observations and simulations of cloud properties within aerosol plumes.
